sections.title: Headline
sections.content: The latest available daily batch in the configured biology/biomedicine arXiv corpus is dated 2026-11-12: 8 eligible papers (7 new submissions and 1 revision). Protein-model reliability and mutation-effect prediction are the clearest shared thread, alongside low-field fMRI, red-cell mechanics, and decision-support methods. The spoken agenda is to examine how protein models are tested, then compare translational claims with the evidence reported. arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred relevance ranking from incomplete biomedical coverage.

sections.title: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects
sections.abstract: The authors combine structure-based energy estimates, protein-language-model scores, and inverse-folding scores into a PDB-scale mutation resource, then train a disagreement-aware preference model evaluated on ProteinGym.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report 15.9 million residue positions across 86,479 chains and zero-shot evaluation on 201 ProteinGym datasets; their disagreement-aware model reaches macro Spearman 0.498, above the evaluated baselines. These are computational predictions and benchmark correlations, not new mutation assays.
sections.unique_caveat: Most augmentation signals are generated computationally (including FoldX); benchmark correlation does not establish experimental performance for a new protein or clinical variant.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct protein-variant relevance; arXiv notes acceptance at ICML 2026, corroborated by the PMLR proceedings and ICML poster listing. No popularity claim is inferred.

sections.title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
sections.abstract: The authors globally permute amino-acid labels without changing alignment statistics and report that contact maps from several protein language models change sharply, unlike the tested Potts and inverse-covariance methods.
sections.claimed_contribution: Across ESM-2, MSA Transformer, and AMPLIFY, the authors report contact-map degradation after relabeling and argue that canonical amino-acid identities, not only coevolutionary statistics, influence these predictions. Their paper reports tests across nine proteins and three seeds for a central ESM-2 comparison.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors note a limited set of short proteins/families, readouts, and model families; relabeling invariance is necessary but not sufficient evidence of pure coevolutionary inference. This is a computational diagnostic, not a claim that contact predictions are unusable.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Directly tests a key interpretation of protein-model outputs; arXiv records acceptance at the ICBINB workshop at NeurIPS 2026, also listed on the NeurIPS workshop page.

sections.title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
sections.abstract: This review proposes describing biological foundation-model reliability through five design elements—data, architecture, training, evaluation, and post-analysis—and links these boundaries to agentic workflows.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors offer a conceptual framework for stating where biological foundation models and agentic systems can be relied on, illustrated through literature on sequences, structures, single-cell, and other omics data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review/perspective rather than a prospective benchmark or new experimental study; the proposed framework still needs operational testing across real biological tasks.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad fit to computational biology and model-evaluation practice; the arXiv comment says it is to be published in Annual Review of Biomedical Data Science.

sections.title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
sections.abstract: The paper models how a hit-centered second-generation DNA-encoded library (DEL) might need to sample chemical space to provide enough tight binders and local affinity variation for training a high-resolution binding model.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use an “energy pixels” abstraction and affinity spread from a naive library to estimate a required library complexity and a baseline expected yield for a randomly designed follow-up DEL.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract describes an estimation framework, not a prospective library synthesis or experimental binding validation; predicted library requirements should be checked against measured compounds and affinities.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Clear molecular-discovery and biomolecule-modeling relevance; the available evidence is the new primary-category listing and paper abstract, with no independent attention signal used.

sections.title: Stretched bilayer-cytoskeleton links hold echinocytes in a model splenic slit
sections.abstract: In a two-component red-cell model, stage III echinocytes required much higher pressure drops than discocytes to pass a model splenic slit, with near-fully stretched bilayer–cytoskeleton links implicated in the hold.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report model simulations in which stage III echinocytes were held at 37–50 times the pressure drop that passed a discocyte; lengthening the modeled links about twofold released held cells in most test runs.
sections.unique_caveat: The central evidence is computational and the model links do not break; this is not direct validation in perfused human spleens or evidence about transfusion outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Strong direct cell-biophysics relevance and cross-listing in q-bio.CB; ranking rests on the paper’s reported mechanistic model results rather than readership evidence.

sections.title: A risk-aware individualized blood pressure target to avoid hypotension in surgery
sections.abstract: The authors propose an online model to choose a MAP target and norepinephrine dose under a stated risk bound, then assess calibration retrospectively and in a virtual-patient cohort.
sections.claimed_contribution: At a nominal 5% risk threshold the method recommended a dose for 74% of virtual patients; 6.9% of those with recommendations had a MAP reading below 65 mmHg. The fixed 70-mmHg comparison reports 25% over the full virtual cohort.
sections.unique_caveat: This is retrospective/model-based evaluation, not a prospective clinical trial; the recommendation subset and full-cohort comparator are not identical populations. It is not evidence of clinical benefit or a treatment recommendation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct biomedical decision-method relevance; the abstract reports a 4,096-virtual-patient evaluation and comparison with a fixed-target baseline. No independent attention signal was verified.

sections.title: A Feasibility Study of Whole-Cerebrum Task-Based fMRI at 0.55 T: Motor and Visual Tasks Using Single-Shot EPI
sections.abstract: In six healthy participants, the authors report detectable task fMRI activations at 0.55 T and improved sensitivity with longer acquisitions, with a representative 3 T dataset as reference context.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report FWE-corrected task activations at 0.55 T and a 47% reduction in voxelwise dispersion after combining two runs; they conclude that longer low-field scans may offset some sensitivity loss in this setup.
sections.unique_caveat: Six healthy volunteers and a representative 3 T reference do not establish general clinical equivalence, diagnostic accuracy, or patient benefit.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct medical-physics relevance; the primary abstract reports six participants and a within-session comparison of 5- versus 10-minute acquisitions.

sections.title: Symmetry-Induced Conservation Laws, Three-Channel Attribution, and Solid-Phase Recycling in Prebiotic Enantiomeric Excess Amplification
sections.abstract: The authors formalize how phase removal, subpool fractionation, and chiral-excess changes contribute to enantiomeric excess, and re-analyze prebiotic chemistry benchmarks under explicit symmetry assumptions.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors state that their accounting framework distinguishes apparent enrichment caused by mass removal from net chiral-excess change, and report re-analysis of seven experimental systems plus model/data-set analyses. These are the authors’ theoretical and re-analysis claims.
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusions depend on the stated network and symmetry assumptions; the abstract reports re-analysis and modeling rather than new wet-lab validation. The version change is labeled as a revision, not a new paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A revision in the selected batch and direct biochemical/prebiotic-chemistry relevance; no independent attention signal was used to rank it.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.content: Protein-model behavior and mutation-effect prediction recur in MutAtlas, the amino-acid relabeling diagnostic, and the hit-centered DEL design paper. They address different tasks and do not independently validate one another; the Cai et al. review provides a broader framework for model reliability. A smaller biomedical-methods thread spans low-field fMRI, virtual-patient blood-pressure modeling, and red-cell mechanics simulation, but their evidence types differ and do not establish clinical readiness.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.content: Follow up MutAtlas with prospective deep-mutational-scanning assays on held-out protein families; broaden the relabeling diagnostic across families, architectures, and retrained checkpoints; and test DEL sizing predictions by synthesizing hit-centered libraries at several complexities. For biomedical methods, use a larger matched 0.55 T/3 T fMRI cohort, prospective controlled evaluation of the blood-pressure method with matched comparators, and shape-sorted red-cell experiments in slit-like devices that directly assess bilayer–cytoskeleton strain. These are proposals grounded in reported evidence boundaries, not clinical recommendations.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Protein-model diagnostics and mutation-effect prediction are the strongest repeated thread in this batch, but the evidence does not support an arXiv-wide popularity ranking. The biomedical studies span simulation, retrospective/virtual cohorts, and six-person feasibility imaging; none establishes clinical benefit. Verify computational predictions and human-facing claims in the specific validation settings where they would be used.
